summary.title: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World

details: Interactive world models must simultaneously keep persistent memory, respond at interactive latency, and run for long horizons, but retaining history in the denoiser context/KV cache makes per-step cost grow with session length, and a few-step distilled generator can only inherit the temporal horizon and conditioning behavior its teacher was trained to express.

Evoke, a three-step CFG-free video world model built on a bounded recurrent interface: each step generates a 1.5s chunk from a fixed-size local history, a per-chunk text condition, and geometry read from an external camera-pose-indexed 'world state bank' (generated frames lifted to depth/point geometry, re-rendered into the current view as pixel-space warp conditioning with a visibility mask), so context and positional range never grow with session duration.

Its second pillar treats the distillation teacher as a design variable rather than a fixed high-quality scorer: a chunk-wise sparsely-attending teacher (local context + retrieved distant frames + linear-attention global state, giving linear cost) with independent per-chunk text conditions, enabling a ~30s full-window distribution-matching objective over self-forced student rollouts that transfers long-range consistency and mid-session prompt responsiveness ('evocation') to the few-step student.
Design separation: long-horizon teacher supervision governs temporal content evolution, while the external pose-addressed geometric store handles spatial revisit consistency.

Student initialized from Helios, progressively trained for camera-controllable then few-step generation, then long-distill + short post-distill; trained on the Sekai video dataset plus internal video.

Teacher adapted from the 14B Wan2.2 A14B diffusion transformer, keeping its high-/low-noise experts; the critic is the same backbone with a LoRA adapter enabled, so teacher and critic scores share an expert.

Chunk = 9 latent frames = 36 pixel frames = 1.5s at 24fps; inference at 384x640 with three CFG-free evaluations over a coarse-to-fine latent pyramid (12x20, 24x40, 48x80), geometry injected only at the coarsest stage.

Rollout: 1 ground-truth prefix chunk + 20 self-forced generated chunks = 189 latent frames (~31.4s, 753 pixel frames); 60 student forward passes per rollout; teacher and critic score the entire 189-frame window jointly.

DMD gradient (normalized score difference) masked to exclude the GT prefix and the first generated chunk to avoid first-frame-distribution boundary flicker; history detached between chunks so the gradient horizon is one chunk while the supervision horizon is the full rollout.

Per-chunk text conditioning: training captions segmented at 12s intervals and mapped to latent chunks, exposing prompt transitions inside one sequence; auxiliary supervised warp-conditioning loss retained as a camera-controllability regularizer; sequence parallelism (Ulysses) and activation recomputation; long-distill on 6x8 GPUs.
Write: Depth Anything 3 depth on 12 frames per generated chunk, unprojected with known intrinsics/extrinsics; chunks inserted independently to avoid cross-sequence depth scale drift.

Read: stored source views ranked by co-visibility with the target pose, up to 8 distinct sources rendered by batched projection with z-buffering, returning a warped view plus per-pixel visibility; visibility<0.5 gets sigma=1 (no information), supported pixels sigma in [0,0.135], and unsupported history tokens are pruned from the sequence.
Budgets: student local history of 19 latent frames (~3.2s) in 16/2/1 long/mid/short tiers; retention of 2160 pixel frames (90s), every third frame ingested, so at most 720 active source frames.

WBench navigation split (158 cases) against eight few-step interactive systems (e.g. Yume-1.5, Matrix-Game 2.0, HunyuanWorld 1.5, Hunyuan-GameCraft, Genie 3, Lingbot); VBench-2.0 and VBench-Long against many-step leaderboard systems (declared protocol deviations: single sample per prompt, shorter clips, prompt augmentation).

Long-session tests: eight uninterrupted 65.5-minute rollouts (2,619 chunks, 94,281 frames each) on a single H200 at 384x640 with no KV caching/compilation/quantization, plus two-hour qualitative rollouts; photometric statistics and content descriptors compared against real-video controls.

Targeted probes: revisit PSNR between two 12s windows at identical poses across leave-and-return trajectories with varying retention vs time-away; mid-session prompt 'evocation' realization rates; wall-clock decomposition of the geometric path.
Matched-recipe students distilled from a short-horizon vs the long-horizon Evoke teacher.

Sweep of the scoring/supervision window W (13 controlled perturbation conditions, varying perturbation-to-scored-chunk distance) to test a window-length detectability explanation; score-noise analysis over 5,749 logged training steps.
Per-chunk teacher conditioning replaced by a single global prompt with W held fixed.

key_findings.finding: Externalizing world state into a bounded, pose-indexed geometric bank yields open-ended generation whose per-step cost and context do not grow with session length.
key_findings.evidence: Eight uninterrupted 65.5-minute rollouts (2,619 chunks, 94,281 frames) on one H200 at 384x640 show stable per-step cost once the 90s retention budget fills; each 1.5s chunk is denoised in 2.11s; photometric statistics stabilize after an initial transient with little later drift, and content descriptors decorrelate at rates comparable to real-video controls, indicating no runaway degradation (interpreted as absence of runaway drift, not permanent identity preservation).

key_findings.finding: A three-step, CFG-free student can match or lead many-step systems on interactive world-model and general video benchmarks.
key_findings.evidence: Leads Video Quality, Setting, and Physical group averages among evaluated few-step systems on the 158-case WBench navigation split and is on par with the best in Consistency, and tops the public WBench leaderboard for that split by 0.1 average despite three steps and no CFG; scores 66.77 on VBench-2.0 and 85.11 on VBench-Long.

key_findings.finding: Extending the teacher's supervision horizon transfers measurably better long-rollout photometric stability to the few-step student, but the demonstrated gain is limited to photometric stability.
key_findings.evidence: Two students distilled with identical recipes from short- vs long-horizon teachers: the long-teacher student shows substantially stronger photometric stability across paired long rollouts, while the content descriptor does not separate them, sharpness does not improve, and the post-distill checkpoint shows no additional drift advantage.

key_findings.finding: The teacher-horizon benefit cannot be reduced to simply making drift detectable within a longer scoring window.
key_findings.evidence: Across 13 controlled perturbation conditions, teacher-critic detectability changes little once the window exceeds W=2 chunks and no consistent sharp threshold appears as W grows or as perturbation-to-scored-chunk distance varies; over 5,749 logged training steps, per-evaluation stochastic variation is large relative to the systematic drift component.

key_findings.finding: Pose-addressed geometric recall restores information only when the retention window covers the time spent away, and returns recognizable rather than pixel-faithful content.
key_findings.evidence: Revisit PSNR between identically posed 12s windows: 20 of 21 controlled comparisons follow the predicted transition, retention windows at least as long as the time away score 2.3-3.2 dB higher than shorter ones, with a 15.4-17.8 dB plateau; recall stays near the same-run far-pose floor when retention is shorter than the absence.
